around.headline: Two terror suspects arrested in Karnataka
around.summary: Karnataka police arrested two terror suspects, per The Times of India. No public advisory has followed, but it's a reminder to report unattended bags or suspicious activity at transit hubs to the police helpline.

around.headline: Toll booths may vanish as Bengaluru highways go fully cashless
around.summary: Bengaluru's highway toll plazas are moving toward fully cashless collection, phasing out physical booths, per Bangalore Mirror. If you drive on tolled stretches regularly, make sure your FASTag is active and adequately recharged.

around.headline: Faulty traffic signals leaving Bengaluru's traffic police stuck in manual mode
around.summary: Malfunctioning signals at several junctions are forcing traffic police to manage flow manually for longer stretches, exposing them to heat and pollution, per The Hindu. Expect less predictable signal timing at affected junctions — watch the road, not just the light.

around.headline: SIR deadline closing in: 90% of 43 lakh exclusion notices delivered in Karnataka
around.summary: Ninety percent of the 43 lakh notices under the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls have been delivered across Karnataka as the correction deadline nears, per The Times of India. If you haven't checked your name on the draft roll yet — especially given the disproportionate deletions already flagged in several Bengaluru seats — do it before the window shuts.

around.headline: Nandini milk price may rise by Rs 5 a litre; CM's call expected today
around.summary: The price of Nandini milk could go up by Rs 5 per litre, with the Chief Minister expected to decide today, per The Times of India. Worth factoring into the monthly grocery budget if the hike is confirmed.

around.headline: Centre pays employees' salary in advance ahead of a 3-day bank strike
around.summary: Central government employees received their salary in advance on September 25 because of an upcoming 3-day bank strike, per People Matters HR News. If you bank with a public-sector lender, withdraw any cash you need and avoid depending on a branch visit over the next few days.

street_smart.title: You're flat-hunting in Bengaluru and find one that's perfect for your budget. The broker says three other people are interested and asks you to pay a ₹10,000 'token advance' in cash right now, before showing you the rental agreement or letting you meet the landlord, to hold the flat.
street_smart.based_on: No incident in today's feeds gave a choice-based personal trap with enough detail (today's real Bengaluru stories — a tragic murder disguised as a prank, a hiring-discrimination row, faulty traffic signals and a milk-price hike — are either tragedies, controversies or civic/administrative news rather than a personal decision point). Rotating in 'rental agreement traps' from the evergreen list: this mechanism hasn't appeared as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: You're relocating for work and need to finalise a place within a couple of days, so the pressure to decide fast feels real.

choices.text: Pay the ₹10,000 in cash immediately, since good flats in your budget don't stay available for long.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Cash paid with no receipt and no landlord contact is unrecoverable if the flat turns out to be already rented, doesn't exist, or the broker vanishes — a well-known Bengaluru rental scam runs exactly this way, collecting 'token advances' from several hopeful renters for the same unit.

choices.text: Agree to pay a token amount, but only against a signed receipt (amount, date, purpose, broker's name and phone number), and insist on meeting the landlord or seeing proof of ownership (a property tax receipt or sale deed) and the draft rental agreement before or right after paying.
choices.feedback: Correct. A receipt gives you a paper trail if the deal falls through, meeting the landlord confirms the flat and broker are genuine, and reading the agreement first lets you check the deposit-refund terms and notice period before any money changes hands — a legitimate broker or landlord won't object to any of this.

choices.text: Refuse to pay anything until the full agreement is signed, and walk away to keep looking elsewhere.
choices.feedback: Risky. Many genuine landlords do ask for a small, receipted token to hold a listing while paperwork is drawn up — refusing outright and walking away every time means losing good, legitimate options unnecessarily. Verify instead of automatically avoiding.

choices.text: Ask a friend to transfer the amount to the broker's personal UPI ID instead of paying cash, since at least there's a digital trail.
choices.feedback: Risky. A UPI trail is better than untraceable cash, but it still doesn't establish who the broker is, whether the landlord exists, or what the money was actually for — you need a receipt and landlord verification regardless of payment method.

takeaways: Never hand over any advance — cash, UPI or otherwise — without a signed, dated receipt naming the broker or landlord and stating the purpose of the payment.

Verify the landlord's identity and ownership (a property tax receipt, electricity bill, or sale deed) before paying anything beyond a token amount, and read the deposit-refund and notice-period clauses in the agreement first.

A rental agreement above 11 months should be registered; for anything shorter, still get it printed on stamp paper and signed by both parties — a verbal promise or WhatsApp chat has no legal standing if the deposit is disputed later.

quiz.question: As of today's report, what share of the 43 lakh exclusion notices under Karnataka's ongoing voter-roll revision (SIR) have been delivered?
quiz.why: The Special Intensive Revision is a door-to-door re-verification of the electoral roll; several Bengaluru assembly seats have already reported unusually high deletion rates during the exercise.

quiz.question: What change is Bengaluru's highway toll system moving toward, according to today's report?
options: Fully cashless collection, phasing out physical booths
Conversion of toll roads to free state highways
Handing toll collection to the BBMP
quiz.why: Barrier-free, camera- or FASTag-based tolling is meant to cut the congestion that builds up at physical toll booths during peak hours.

quiz.question: Why did central government employees receive their salary in advance on September 25?
options: A cybersecurity upgrade at public-sector banks
quiz.why: Advancing salaries ahead of a multi-day bank strike is a routine step so that employees aren't left without access to funds while branches are shut or short-staffed.

quiz.question: Under India's Constitution, which list contains subjects like police and public order, on which only state legislatures can make laws?
quiz.why: The Concurrent List, by contrast, holds subjects like education and forests where both Parliament and state legislatures can legislate, with central law prevailing in case of conflict.

quiz.question: What term describes a market where a single seller controls the entire supply of a good or service?
quiz.why: A monopsony is the mirror-image situation — a market with only one buyer rather than one seller, such as a single large employer in a small town's job market.
